titulo: Tao Te Ching, chapter 1, on a Saturday
caption:
Tao Te Ching, chapter 1, in three ordinary moments.
“The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.” Lao Tzu, in James Legge’s 1891 translation (public domain).
Link in bio.
by NMR
#taoteching #laotzu #taoism

alt.1: lavender field, Cella saying “Me? Enlightened.” in a speech bubble. Tao Te Ching, chapter 1. 3 Saturday moments you already lived. Written 2,000+ years ago. Still about your Saturday.
alt.2: amber field, Cella at a table saying “Long story.”. The way: “The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.”. You explained your whole life to a friend. It sounded smaller.
alt.3: pink field, Cella next to a phone, saying “I’m a vibe.”. The name: “The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.”. Your bio: six words. Your whole self, apparently.
alt.4: blue field, a big orange sun on the right, a pale yellow Cella looking at a phone and saying “Posted.”. The want: “But if desire always within us be, / Its outer fringe is all that we shall see.”. You photographed the sunset. You saw your phone.
alt.5: the three parts as a list. Tao Te Ching 1, Legge’s 1891 translation: Send it to the friend with the five-year plan. 1. The way · say it and it shrinks. 2. The name · the label fits nothing. 3. The want · wanting shows the edge.
